chapter: Gulf Coast bands and early jobs
title: Playing piano at the Point Clear Hotel and catching the drummer's sticks
summary: His first piano job was Point Clear in 1926; he became a drummer by catching a bad drummer's thrown sticks, and later filled in with the Dukes of Dixieland.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Oh, yes. Fairhope? Oh, that was the first. Fairhope, the old Point Clear Hotel in Fairhope was the first piano job that I had in my life. And I played at the Point Clear Hotel in Fairhope. That was in 1926. I played drums five years before. Almost five years. How I began to play drums was the fact that some, they were organizing a little band in Long Beach where I was living and going to school, going to high school. And a drummer, not a drummer, a guy bought a set of drums to play in the band and he couldn't play to save his life. He played waltz time backwards. Instead of playing dah, he played dah, It was like a sign.

So one night, he says, anybody that can catch these GD sticks when I throw them up in the air can have my set of drums. When he threw them up in the air, I caught both of them, and I played drums from that time on because I was born to keep time with music. Don't you see? Keep the beat. And one night, Roger Johnson got a heart attack in the Dukes, and I saved the night. I played drums with the Dukes of Dixieland, with their original Dukes, you know, their Santo boys.
That's incredible. It came right back to you, enough to keep the beat going?
It never does leave you. If it's there originally, if you're born with it, it never leaves you. Now you may be rusty at it. But all it needed was somebody to keep time.
